cards.explanation: The answer is a lamentation. Amos says it himself: “…this lamentation I take up against you…” A lamentation is a song of mourning, so he isn't coming with a pep talk. He's grieving out loud over the house of Israel, friends. You don't clap along to this one.

The answer is no one. Amos says, “She lies abandoned on her land, with no one to raise her up.” Picture reaching for a hand and finding empty air. That's the whole scene, and it's a heavy one. The passage calls it a lamentation, and I think that's why it sounds so sorrowful.

The answer is a hundred. The LORD says, “The city that marches out a thousand strong will have but a hundred left…” That's one out of every ten still standing. It's a hard number to hear, friends. Those little words “but a” carry a lot.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “…the one that marches out a hundred strong will have but ten left in the house of Israel.” Smaller city, smaller number, same shape. Both lose nine out of every ten, bakers.

The answer is “Seek Me and live.” That's what the LORD says to the house of Israel: “Seek Me and live!” After all that mourning, He opens a door. Notice it's an invitation, friends, not another threat.

The answer is that Gilgal will go into exile and Bethel will come to nothing. The LORD says, “…Gilgal will surely go into exile, and Bethel will come to nothing.” Those are the places He just warned them not to seek or go to. Seeking them leads nowhere. He wants them to seek Him instead.

The answer is fire. The LORD says, “…He will sweep like fire through the house of Joseph…” That's a serious warning, and it says the fire “…will devour everything…” Seeking Him is the way to live. I think that's why the call to seek Him comes right before it.
The answer is False. The fire “…will devour everything, with no one at Bethel to extinguish it.” So there's no one at Bethel to put it out. The only safe move, friends, is to seek the LORD.

The answer is True. It's all one sentence about one Person. “He who made the Pleiades and Orion…” also “…summons the waters of the sea and pours them over the face of the earth…” and the verse ends, “…the LORD is His name…” Star groups overhead, the sea below, and He handles both. That's who Amos says is speaking.
The answer is True. The verse says, “He flashes destruction on the strong, so that fury comes upon the stronghold.” A stronghold is a place built to be safe. Walls don't stop Him here, friends.

The answer is that they will never live in them. The LORD says, “…you will never live in the stone houses you have built…” The reason in the text is that they trample on the poor and exact a tax of grain from him. They did all that building and don't get to move in. Think of paying for the whole house and never getting a key.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “you will never drink the wine from the lush vineyards you have planted.” Same pattern as the stone houses. They put in all that work and don't get to enjoy the wine.

The answer is by taking bribes. The LORD says, “You oppress the righteous by taking bribes…” A bribe is a payment to tilt a decision. It goes straight against the integrity verse 10 mentions, friends.

The answer is False, and the text is clear. The LORD says, “you deprive the poor of justice in the gate.” The place where they should find justice is the place they're shut out. Later He tells them to “establish justice in the gate.” (Amos 5:15).

The answer is True. Verse 13 says, “Therefore, the prudent keep silent in such times, for the days are evil.” So the prudent stay quiet. Sometimes silence is the loudest sign of how heavy the times are, friends.

The answer is that He will be with them. The LORD says, “…the LORD, the God of Hosts, will be with you, as you have claimed.” After all those warnings, here is a promise to be with them. That's the best thing on the whole table. Seek good and you live.

The answer is justice. The LORD says, “Hate evil and love good; establish justice in the gate.” Back in verse 7 there were those who turned justice into wormwood, so this is the reverse. The gate is where the poor were being denied it. Now He tells them to put it back.

The answer is the remnant of Joseph. The verse says, “Perhaps the LORD, the God of Hosts, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.” A remnant is what's left. It's a small word with a lot of hope in it, friends.
The answer is True. The verse says, “The farmer will be summoned to mourn, and the mourners to wail.” Even the farmer gets called in. The grief reaches wide, friends.

The answer is that He will pass through their midst. The LORD says, “There will be wailing in all the vineyards, for I will pass through your midst…” says the LORD. That's the reason, right in His own words. It's a sobering line, friends.
